deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.1 夢 — Grammar & Expressions
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第一章「夢」
notes: Grammar, literary devices and Itomori dialect for Chapter 1. The opening-page cards (p.5) are checked against the printed page, and the words you wrote in your notebook are tagged flagged_in_notebook. The rest — 三葉's morning, the comet on the news, the twilight lesson in class, braiding cords with her grandmother, and the shrine ritual — is built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style, not copied out page by page, so a few words may turn up a chapter early or late. Example sentences are original, not quoted from the book.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

meanings: ending a sentence on a noun
cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the waking sequence is a chain of one-noun sentences: ceiling, room, morning, alone, Tokyo.
cards.context: Form: … Noun。 — the sentence stops on a noun with no だ/です and no verb. It works like quick camera cuts: each noun is a snapshot. Read them as 'There's the …' / 'It's …'. 新海誠 uses it constantly.
cards.example_sentence: 夏の夜。静かな湖。遠くで聞こえる祭りの音。
cards.example_reading: なつ の よる。 しずかな みずうみ。 とおく で きこえる まつり の おと。
cards.example_meaning: A summer night. A still lake. The sound of a festival far away.

meanings: present tense used to narrate events
cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — 目が開く, くっついている — the narration is in the present tense.
cards.context: Form: dictionary / 〜ている forms in narration, mixed with 〜た. Present tense puts you inside the moment, like watching a film. Shifting to 〜た often signals looking back or a step outside the moment. In English you can usually translate either way.
cards.example_sentence: 電車が止まる。ドアが開く。私は一歩、外に出た。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ が とまる。 ドア が ひらく。 わたし は いっぽ、 そと に でた。
cards.example_meaning: The train stops. The doors open. I stepped outside.
cards.pattern: Dictionary form / 〜ている in narration (instead of 〜た)

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — two people bound so closely they can hardly be separated (分かちがたく).
cards.context: Form: Vます-stem + がたい (also written 難い). Unlike 〜にくい (physically or practically hard), 〜がたい means you can't bring yourself to, emotionally or morally: 信じがたい (hard to believe), 忘れがたい (unforgettable), 許しがたい (unforgivable). Written, literary register.
cards.example_sentence: あの夏の日々は、今でも忘れがたい思い出だ。
cards.example_reading: あの なつ の ひび は、 いま でも わすれがたい おもいで だ。
cards.example_meaning: Those summer days are still a memory I can hardly forget.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — 隙間なく — pressed together with no gap at all.
cards.context: Form: Noun + なく — the adverb form of 'there is no N'. 隙間なく (with no gaps), 休みなく (without a break), 迷いなく (without hesitation), 間もなく (soon — lit. 'with no interval'). More written than 〜がなくて or 〜なしで.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は迷いなく答えを書いた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は まよい なく こたえ を かいた。
cards.example_meaning: She wrote her answer without hesitation.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — 不安や寂しさなんて — anxiety, loneliness, any of that: none at all.
cards.context: Form: Noun / plain form + なんて. Puts a feeling on the thing named — usually dismissive (宿題なんて = homework, ugh), sometimes amazed (彼が来るなんて! = I can't believe he's coming!). Casual, emotional cousin of など.
cards.example_sentence: 宿題なんて、明日やればいいよ。
cards.example_reading: しゅくだい なんて、 あした やれば いい よ。
cards.example_meaning: Homework? You can just do it tomorrow.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — 寂しさ — loneliness, from 寂しい.
cards.context: Form: い-adj stem + さ (寂しい → 寂しさ, 高い → 高さ); な-adj + さ (静か → 静かさ). Turns a quality into a noun you can talk about or measure. 〜み (甘み, 痛み) is closer to the felt sensation.
cards.example_sentence: 一人になって、友だちの大切さが分かった。
cards.example_reading: ひとり に なって、 ともだち の たいせつさ が わかった。
cards.example_meaning: Being alone, I understood how precious friends are.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — no anxiety or loneliness — not a shred (なんてかけらもない).
cards.context: Form: Noun + のかけらもない (or Noun + なんてかけらもない). Emphatic 'zero': 優しさのかけらもない (not a shred of kindness), 反省のかけらもない (not the least bit sorry). かけら = fragment.
cards.example_sentence: あの人の言葉には、思いやりのかけらもなかった。
cards.example_reading: あの ひと の ことば に は、 おもいやり の かけら も なかった。
cards.example_meaning: There wasn't a shred of consideration in what that person said.

cards.scene: The opening compares the dream to being a nursing baby (〜のように); まるで often leads such comparisons in 新海誠's narration.
cards.context: Form: まるで + N の / plain form + ように (adverb) / ような (before a noun); casual: みたいに / みたいな. まるで flags a striking comparison: まるで夢のようだ.
cards.example_sentence: 雪の朝、町はまるで絵のように静かだった。
cards.example_reading: ゆき の あさ、 まち は まるで え の よう に しずか だった。
cards.example_meaning: On the snowy morning, the town was as still as a painting.
cards.pattern: まるで + N の / plain form + ように・ような

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — ——そうか。 After waking, the narrator realises what's going on.
cards.context: Form: plain form + のだ / んだ. In narration, especially right after そうか, のだ marks the moment something clicks: 'So that's it — I was dreaming.' Elsewhere it explains or emphasises. 〜のだった adds a reflective, looking-back feel.
cards.example_sentence: そうか、あれは全部夢だったのだ。
cards.example_reading: そう か、 あれ は ぜんぶ ゆめ だった の だ。
cards.example_meaning: I see — it was all a dream.
cards.pattern: Plain form + のだ / んだ

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — ——そうか。 The moment the waking dreamer understands.
cards.context: Form: そうか (plain), そっか (casual), そうですか (polite). Falling tone = 'oh, I see / so that's it'; rising tone = 'really?'. In narration, ——そうか。 marks the click of understanding.
cards.example_sentence: 「明日は休みだよ。」「そっか、祝日だったね。」
cards.example_reading: 「あした は やすみ だ よ。」 「そっか、 しゅくじつ だった ね。」
cards.example_meaning: 'Tomorrow's a day off.' 'Oh right, it's a holiday.'
cards.pattern: そうか / そっか (plain) · そうですか (polite)

cards.reading: にいちど / にいっぽん
cards.scene: The comet comes round only once in a very long cycle — and in a small town, lots of things come 'once every…'.
cards.context: Form: [time span] + に + [count]. 千年に一度 (once every thousand years), 一時間に一本 (one bus/train an hour), 週に三回 (three times a week). The counter changes with the thing counted: 本 for trains and buses, 度/回 for events.
cards.example_sentence: このバスは、一時間に一本しか来ない。
cards.example_reading: この バス は、 いちじかん に いっぽん しか こない。
cards.example_meaning: This bus only comes once an hour.
cards.pattern: Time span + に + 一度 / 一回 / 一本 …

cards.scene: News about the comet: its first close pass in an enormously long time.
cards.context: Form: [time span] + ぶり (に / の). 三年ぶりに会った (met for the first time in three years); 千年ぶりの接近 (the first approach in a thousand years). Don't mix it up with 〜ぶり meaning 'manner': 話しぶり (way of talking).
cards.example_sentence: 五年ぶりに故郷の駅に降りた。
cards.example_reading: ごねん ぶり に こきょう の えき に おりた。
cards.example_meaning: I got off at my hometown station for the first time in five years.
cards.pattern: Time span + ぶり(に / の)

cards.scene: News and gossip about the comet: what everyone has heard.
cards.context: Form: plain form + らしい (N / な-adj drop だ). Information you got from someone else or the news. Different from 〜らしい meaning 'typical of' (男らしい) and from 〜そうだ (a more direct report of what was said).
cards.example_sentence: 今夜は、彗星がよく見えるらしい。
cards.example_reading: こんや は、 すいせい が よく みえる らしい。
cards.example_meaning: Apparently the comet will be easy to see tonight.

cards.scene: Friends' chatter and gossip, passing on what someone said.
cards.context: Form: plain form / N + って = と / という / と言っていた. 来ないって = (they said) they're not coming. As a topic: 彗星って何? = what's a comet, anyway? Very common in dialogue.
cards.example_sentence: サヤちん、明日は来られないって。
cards.example_reading: サヤちん、 あした は こられない って。
cards.example_meaning: Saya-chin says she can't come tomorrow.

cards.scene: Itomori characters swap だ for や all the time — 三葉 included, especially when she's upset.
cards.context: Form: Noun / な-adjective + や. 嫌や (= 嫌だ), そうや (= そうだ), 何や (= 何だ), 〜やった (= だった), 〜やない (= じゃない). Typical of western Japan (Kansai, Gifu/Hida). Itomori's speech is modelled on 飛騨弁.
cards.example_sentence: もう、こんな雨の日は嫌や。
cards.example_reading: もう、 こんな あめ の ひ は いや や。
cards.example_meaning: Ugh, I hate rainy days like this.

cards.scene: Family and friends in Itomori use 〜とる for 〜ている — 'what are you doing?' becomes 何しとるの?
cards.context: Form: 〜ている → 〜とる (from 〜ておる). 何しとるの? (= 何しているの?), 知っとる (= 知っている), 見とった (= 見ていた). After a voiced て it becomes 〜どる: 読んどる (= 読んでいる).
cards.example_sentence: お母さん、台所で何しとるの？
cards.example_reading: おかあさん、 だいどころ で なに しとる の？
cards.example_meaning: Mum, what are you doing in the kitchen?

cards.scene: Itomori speech makes verbs negative with 〜ん: 知らん, 分からん.
cards.context: Form: Vない-stem + ん. 知らん (= 知らない), 分からん (= 分からない), 行かん (= 行かない), せん (= しない), こん (= 来ない). Not the explanatory ん of 〜んだ — check what comes before it.
cards.example_sentence: そんな話、ぜんぜん知らん。
cards.example_reading: そんな はなし、 ぜんぜん しらん。
cards.example_meaning: I've never heard anything like that.

meanings: probably / right? (= だろう / でしょう)
cards.scene: Itomori teens use 〜やろ to guess or to ask for agreement.
cards.context: Form: plain form + やろ. そうやろ? (right?), 来るやろ (they'll probably come). Rising tone = 'isn't it?'; falling tone = a guess. 〜やろか = だろうか (I wonder).
cards.example_sentence: 明日は晴れるやろ。
cards.example_reading: あした は はれる やろ。
cards.example_meaning: It'll probably be sunny tomorrow.
cards.pattern: Plain form + やろ (= だろう)

cards.scene: Itomori speakers say ええ for いい.
cards.context: Form: いい → ええ. ええよ (= いいよ, sure / OK), ええなあ (= いいなあ, lucky you), もうええ (= もういい, never mind / that's enough). Don't confuse it with the polite 'yes' ええ — tone and context tell them apart.
cards.example_sentence: 東京はええなあ、何でもあって。
cards.example_reading: とうきょう は ええ なあ、 なんでも あって。
cards.example_meaning: Tokyo's so lucky — it's got everything.

meanings: (it) is, you know (= だよ / なんだ)
cards.scene: A sentence ending that marks Itomori speech as 飛騨弁-style, especially in older speakers' explanations.
cards.context: Form: Noun / plain form + (なん)やさ. Roughly だよ or なんだ — explaining or asserting gently: そうやさ (that's right, you know), 決まりなんやさ (it's the rule, you see). Very characteristic of the Hida region.
cards.example_sentence: この祭りは、昔からの決まりなんやさ。
cards.example_reading: この まつり は、 むかし から の きまり なん やさ。
cards.example_meaning: This festival is a custom from long ago, you see.
cards.pattern: Noun / plain form + (なん)やさ (= だよ / なんだ)

cards.scene: More Itomori-style endings: やけど for だけど, やで for だよ.
cards.context: Form: N / な-adj / plain + やけど (= だけど), + やで (= だよ). そうやけど = that's true, but…; 明日やで = it's tomorrow, you know. The same や that replaces だ.
cards.example_sentence: 今日は雨やけど、祭りは明日やで。
cards.example_reading: きょう は あめ やけど、 まつり は あした やで。
cards.example_meaning: It's raining today, but the festival's tomorrow, you know.
cards.pattern: N / plain + やけど (= だけど) · やで (= だよ)
